newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European Union ministers threaten fur import ban.
newsitem.headline: European Union ministers threaten fur import ban.

text.p: European Union environment ministers threatened on Monday to impose an EU import ban on fur from animals caught in leg-hold traps unless negotiators from Canada, the United States and Russia accept tighter humane trapping standards, a statement said.
Ministers told the European Commission "to take the necessary steps as of 1, January 1997 for the introduction of an import ban to come into effect not later than 31 March 1997".

Ministers said they were concerned that draft trapping standards, agreed between the European Commission, Canada and Russia but rejected by Washington, "would allow some some form of leghold traps to continue to be used".

Negotiators from the four sides have been in talks for months over improved trapping standards in an effort to avert a fur import ban already agreed by the EU, preventing the ban coming into force while negotiations continued.
The talks are intended to lay down standards for traps which kill or catch 18 species of wild animals, including muskrats, beavers, sable, lynx and wolves.
A draft text of the humane trapping standards, seen by Reuters, would have required trap killing times for most of the 18 species not to exceed six minutes.

The draft would outlaw steel-jawed leg-hold traps from four years after the deal's entry into force but would leave unclear the phase-out period for restraining traps, which it defined as those which neither kill captured animals nor inflict any of a list of injuries ranging from bone fracture, severe internal organ damage or limb amputation.

Ministers asked in their statement, which Italy rejected, that the Commission reopen talks with the other three parties so as to reach a "more satisfactory agreement", though without specifying details.

National and international animal welfare groups had already damned the draft standards as a "cynical political solution" to U.S. threats of World Trade Organisation retaliation if the EU ban went ahead.
A U.S. official told Reuters on Monday that an agreement on the draft standards had been "quite close".
Demonstrators dressed as bloodstained furry creatures greeted environment ministers as they arrived for their scheduled meeting on Monday.
